- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 7–14 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 7–14 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is mixed or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% for next 5–10 days to compensate for low sentiment bias.
